name: Ascension Salesforce Development Standards
summary: Declarative first; Flow before trigger; triggers via TriggerHandler; bulk-safe, tested Apex.

rules.title: Declarative first
rules.rule: Build with a Flow (or configuration) first. Use Apex or a trigger only when the Flow is too complex or cannot do it, and say why in the spec.

rules.title: No hardcoded IDs
rules.rule: Never hardcode Salesforce record IDs; they change between environments. Limit hardcoded values: use Custom Metadata, Custom Labels, Custom Settings or constants.

rules.title: Keep it simple
rules.rule: Remove unnecessary logic; reuse code through single methods that return a value.

rules.title: Permission sets, not profiles
rules.rule: Grant access with permission sets; never change profiles.

rules.title: Custom object naming
rules.rule: Descriptive names, each word capitalised, no acronyms (unless well known), no work-stream prefix, no underscores in the name. Always give the object a description.

rules.title: Custom field naming
rules.rule: Descriptive, short, each word capitalised, no acronyms, no underscores in the name (API name like NextStepDate__c). Always a description, and help text for the end user.

rules.title: Child relationship naming
rules.rule: Relationship names describe the relationship, each word capitalised (e.g. Contact Sales).

rules.title: Layouts, apps and pages
rules.rule: Descriptive, short, each word capitalised, no 'Layout' suffix.

rules.title: Custom permissions and permission sets
rules.rule: Descriptive, each word capitalised, no underscores in the label, always a description.

rules.title: Validation rule naming
rules.rule: Single field: [Field Label] [rule applied] (Contact First Name Cannot Be Null). Multiple fields: [grouping] [rule applied]. Cross object: [Object] [Field Label] [rule applied]. Always a description and a clear error message on the field.

rules.title: Record type naming
rules.rule: Descriptive, short, each word capitalised, no underscores, always a description of what differentiates it.

rules.title: Static resource naming
rules.rule: All upper case (e.g. JQUERY); minified libraries; zipped in CSS/JS/Images folders with a ReadMe.

rules.title: Flow naming and description
rules.rule: Descriptive label, each word capitalised, no 'Flow' suffix, no underscores in the label, always a description of what the flow does. Variables in camelCase (firstName).

rules.title: Fault paths
rules.rule: Every element that creates, updates, deletes or looks up records has a fault path to an error handler.

rules.title: DML at the end
rules.rule: Place record changes at the end of the flow; keep records processed per batch low.

rules.title: One automation entry per object
rules.rule: Before adding a flow or trigger, check what already runs on the object and extend it rather than adding a competing one where possible.

rules.title: Apex naming
rules.rule: UpperCamelCase nouns for classes, lowerCamelCase for methods and variables, whole words, no one-letter variables, constants in UPPER_CASE. Suffixes: Controller, Ext, Batch, Scheduler, Queueable, Test, TriggerHandler, Helper (avoid), Constant, WebService, Selector, Domain, Service (plural object: AccountsService); interfaces start with Interface.

rules.title: Sharing
rules.rule: Classes declare with sharing (or inherited sharing with a reason).

rules.title: No SOQL or SOSL in loops
rules.rule: Query before the loop (or use a SOQL for-loop over the query) and pass Sets or Lists.

rules.title: No DML in loops
rules.rule: Collect records and do one DML on the collection.

rules.title: Bulkified
rules.rule: All Apex, triggers included, handles 200 records; never use only Trigger.new[0].

rules.title: Exception handling
rules.rule: Wrap DML in try/catch (finally where needed), use Database methods for partial success, savepoints to roll back, and throw meaningful exceptions.

rules.title: Separation of concerns
rules.rule: Use Selector (queries), Domain and Service layers for enterprise logic; keep queries selective and filtered.

rules.title: Asynchronous processing
rules.rule: Use Queueable, Batch (over 50k records) and Scheduled Apex for long-running or large-volume work.

rules.title: Formatting and comments
rules.rule: Lines at most 120 characters; JavaDoc comments on classes and methods; // comments only where code is unclear.

rules.title: One trigger per object, named after the object
rules.rule: Only one trigger per object, named exactly after the object (trigger Account on Account).

rules.title: Logic-free trigger with a handler
rules.rule: The trigger holds no logic: it only runs <ObjectName>TriggerHandler, which extends the org's TriggerHandler framework (bypass and recursion control).

rules.title: Coverage
rules.rule: At least 90% coverage per class; aim for 100%.

rules.title: Meaningful tests
rules.rule: Every test class is <ClassName>Test, asserts behaviour, covers positive and negative cases and bulk (200 records); create data in @TestSetup or a factory; never SeeAllData=true.

rules.title: LWC practice
rules.rule: Reusable, modular components named in camelCase; no business logic in the template; @wire over imperative calls; Lightning Data Service or lightning-record-form for CRUD; return primitives from Apex; inline error messages rather than toasts; base lightning components over custom HTML.
